staff.bio: Dr. Nyeisha DeWitt is a serial entrepreneur, investor, and founder of Oakland Natives Give Back (ONGB). Since launching ONGB in 2008, she has led the organization in reimagining philanthropy and addressing chronic absenteeism in schools, investing nearly $7 million into student success. A former high school dropout turned educator and funder, Dr. DeWitt brings a rare, multi-faceted perspective to this national issue. She holds a B.A. in Sociology from UC Berkeley, an M.A. in Teaching and an Ed.D. in Organization and Leadership from the University of San Francisco, and a Master of Science in Advanced Entrepreneurial Leadership from Babson College.

Dr. Kimberly Mayfield is a respected educator, scholar, and author with over 30 years of experience in K-12 and higher education. She holds two teaching credentials, a master’s in teaching, and a doctorate in Learning and Instruction from the University of San Francisco. Her work focuses on creating a diverse teaching force, reducing chronic absenteeism, and addressing the over-identification of African American students in special education. Dr. Mayfield was the first African American to earn tenure at Holy Names University, where she served in multiple leadership roles. She continues to advise on education policy and provide professional development for school districts across the Bay Area.

Yuri Hernández Osorio (she/her) is the Vice President of Programs at ONGB. Originally from Toluca, México, with roots in Puebla, she brings a strong background in social work, immigration, and equity-centered programming. With a career rooted in higher education, including her recent work at UC Berkeley, Yuri is dedicated to building inclusive systems that support student success. She holds a social work degree from the University of Michigan and enjoys exploring the Bay Area’s vibrant culture, food, and live music scene.

Alaa Abusalah is the Director of Strategy, Innovation, and Partnerships at ONGB, based in Massachusetts. She brings deep experience in strategic planning, project management, and community engagement. Alaa holds a Master’s in Management with a concentration in Advanced Entrepreneurial Leadership from Babson College and a B.A. in Urban Studies from Worcester State University. She has worked across both the public and private sectors, leading initiatives that support schools and agencies in solving chronic absenteeism with innovative, data-driven solutions.

Yumna Usmani is the Director of Operations at ONGB, with global experience in youth development across Pakistan, Peru, Haiti, Nigeria, and the Bay Area. With expertise in operations, program development, and nonprofit management, she is passionate about using technology to streamline and scale mission-driven work. On weekends, she’s planning creative adventures for her two energetic young boys and savoring quiet movie nights when she can.

Mona Blake is a Master’s student in Social Work at Howard University and brings a heart for service and community impact to her work. Driven by empathy and purpose, she’s preparing for a career centered on equity and healing. Outside of her studies, Mona enjoys cooking, gardening, and quality time with her family.

Rahim Harris is an Oakland native with over 15 years of experience supporting youth as a teacher, student support provider, mental health counselor, and case manager. He holds a B.A. in Political Science with a minor in African American Studies from Loyola Marymount University. Rahim is deeply committed to uplifting youth and helping them thrive.

Heather Davis is a driven Oakland native and Program Coordinator at Oakland Natives Give Back, where she designs and manages attendance initiatives that uplift local youth. She’s currently pursuing a degree in Business Operations & Administration at Berkeley City College—and dreaming of joining the Haas School of Business at UC Berkeley next. Outside the office, Heather brings her creativity into the kitchen and studio.

Ana Costa is a Data Scientist at ONGB and a nonprofit director dedicated to advancing equity through sports and education. Originally from the Bugio neighborhood in Brazil, she earned a full athletic scholarship to study in the U.S., completing a B.A. in International Studies with a minor in Political Science, as well as a Business Administration certification from UC Berkeley. She recently earned her M.S. in Data Analytics, specializing in Big Data and Machine Learning, from Georgia State University. Ana has applied her skills across finance, education, and community development, using data-driven strategies to deliver innovative, people-centered solutions for underserved communities.

Erin Gray is the cofounder and alumna of the Girls Equity Movement (GEMS), a flagship initiative of Oakland Natives Give Back that empowers high school girls to become confident changemakers through entrepreneurship, sisterhood, and leadership. A proud graduate of Babson College, Erin combines her passion for education with her entrepreneurial background, working in schools to inspire students who remind her of her own journey as well as still spending investing time and energy to the self-elected, "Refined GEMs". Through GEMS, she is shaping the next generation of innovators, leaders, and trailblazers.

Rodrick Travis is the Facilities Manager at ONGB, where he oversees the safety, functionality, and upkeep of the organization’s physical spaces to support vibrant, community-driven programs. Born and raised in Oakland, he brings extensive experience in operations, logistics, and property management, paired with a deep commitment to creating environments where youth and families can thrive. Rodrick’s dedication to excellence and service reflects ONGB’s mission to uplift the community with care, reliability, and authenticity.

Mia Patterson is a dedicated professional with a background in emergency management, law, and cultural studies. She serves as Executive Personal Assistant to Chief Executive Officer Dr. Nyeisha DeWitt at ONGB. A recent graduate of Northeastern University with a B.A. in History, Culture, and Law, Patterson is committed to the intersection of legal systems and social equity. With over five years of experience as an Emergency Medical Dispatcher and a former dance studio owner, she brings a unique blend of crisis management, youth engagement, and community advocacy to her role.

Carren Gopez holds a bachelor’s degree in Psychology and brings a thoughtful, analytical mindset to her work at ONGB. As a Program Assistant, she primarily supports data-related projects, helping to organize, track, and analyze information that strengthens ONGB’s impact. Her attention to detail and commitment to continuous learning make her a valuable part of the programs team.

Veronica “Nica” Tiamson is an Administrative Professional at ONGB with over 15 years of experience in office management, customer service, HR recruitment, technical support, and sales. Known for her sharp organizational skills and strong communication abilities, she provides high-level executive support and ensures seamless operations through diligence, adaptability, and attention to detail. Nica holds a B.A. in Mass Communication with a major in Broadcast. Outside of work, Nica is a passionate artist who finds joy and purpose in painting.

Maddy Cruz is a Marketing Assistant at ONGB, supporting both the core organization and the Girls Equity Movement (GEMS) program. She brings a creative, client-focused approach to her work, helping to elevate ONGB’s visibility and impact. Outside the office, Maddy stays active through sports and is deeply engaged in outreach efforts, reflecting her passion for community connection and personal growth.

Sandra Garcia is a virtual assistant with international experience supporting clients around the world. She currently serves as Outreach Support at ONGB, where she brings her problem-solving skills, empathy, and professionalism to community engagement efforts. Her human-centered and adaptable approach makes her a reliable ally for teams seeking agility and attention to detail.

Sofía Balardini is a finance professional with a background in investment banking, risk management, and financial analysis. She supports the mission of ONGB as Finance Support, contributing to fiscal planning and strategic financial operations. Balardini has worked with global firms including J.P. Morgan, EY GDS, and Adidas, where she led strategic planning initiatives, operational risk assessments, and project evaluations across local and international markets. She holds a Bachelor's degree in Industrial Engineering and a Master's in Finance from Universidad Torcuato Di Tella. Fluent in English and Spanish, she brings strong analytical acumen, leadership capabilities, and technical proficiency in Excel, SAP, and Microsoft Office tools to every role she undertakes.

Camila Sanchez is a dynamic professional with a background in Bank Administration and Foreign Trade, currently pursuing a specialization in Human Resources. She serves as Administrative Support at ONGB, where she contributes to operational coordination and team support. Her career spans the education, artificial intelligence, and e-commerce sectors, where she has supported business growth, talent development, and operational efficiency. Known for her strategic thinking and adaptability, Sanchez brings a people-first approach to organizational development. She is passionate about building inclusive work environments and aligning HR practices with broader business goals.
